title: Impacts of Piped Water Shortages on Labor Supply: Evidence from Mexico City
abstract: Urban water shortages are an increasingly urgent challenge in large cities, driven by population growth, climate change, and aging infrastructure. In Mexico City—where households lack alternative sources—disruptions to piped supply force residents to either wait at home for public deliveries or spend money on private water trucks and bottled water. These shocks can affect both time and income, creating theoretically ambiguous effects on labor supply. This paper provides novel causal evidence on how piped water shortages affect urban labor supply. I combine high-frequency labor panel data with a proxy that interacts rainfall-driven variation in reservoir storage with each block’s location within Mexico City’s gravity-fed pipeline network. This variation predicts changes in residential water consumption. A drop in reservoir levels from the median to the fifth percentile reduces weekly hours worked by about one hour, on average. Effects are heterogeneous: female formal employees—with access to job protections—reduce hours worked (time effect dominates), while female informal employees increase hours (income effect dominates). These findings highlight how gender roles and job informality mediate labor supply responses to water insecurity in urban settings.
abstract_zh: 城市水资源短缺在大城市中日益成为紧迫的挑战，其驱动因素包括人口增长、气候变化和基础设施老化。在墨西哥城——那里的家庭缺乏替代水源——管道供水中断迫使居民要么在家等待公共配水，要么花钱购买私人送水车和瓶装水。这些冲击会同时影响时间和收入，从而在理论上对劳动供给产生方向不明确的效应。本文提供了关于管道供水短缺如何影响城市劳动供给的新颖因果证据。我结合了高频劳动力面板数据，以及一个代理变量，该变量将降雨驱动的水库蓄水量变化与各街区在墨西哥城重力供水管网中的位置相互作用。这一变量能够预测居民用水量的变化。水库水位从中位数下降至第五百分位数，平均每周工作时长减少约一小时。效应具有异质性：拥有工作保障的女性正式员工减少了工作时长（时间效应占主导），而女性非正式员工则增加了工作时长（收入效应占主导）。这些发现表明，性别角色和工作非正规性如何调节城市环境中劳动供给对水资源不安全的反应。

title: When Do Extraction Rights Help Forests? Robustness and Heterogeneity for Logging Interventions in the Peruvian Amazon
abstract: Large areas of forest are allocated to commercial logging concessions, some of which are eco‐certified. Theoretically, both holding concessions' rights to log and being eco‐certified can increase or decrease forest loss. Impact estimates are sparse and unsurprisingly mixed for these interventions (that aim to affect forest outcomes, if not always for conservation). We ask if adding different forest sensors, forest outcomes, and variations in forest contexts sheds new light upon the forest impacts of uncertified concessions and eco‐certifications. Using new global data, which include forest degradation, we estimate the forest impacts of these interventions within the Peruvian Amazon, disaggregating across timber regions to allow for heterogeneity in impacts across distinct contexts. Our results confirm that, when averaging across the regions, uncertified logging concessions do not increase deforestation (relative to unintervened forest), consistent with previous findings. Yet, separating regions adds insight for policy and external validity: uncertified concessions yield larger reductions in deforestation rates within the more highly pressured of these three core logging regions. Degradation data provide further insights: uncertified concessions did not shift transitions from forest to degraded status, yet reduced transitions from degraded status to deforested. Eco‐certifications did not reduce deforestation or degradation across contexts or outcomes.
abstract_zh: 大片森林被划归商业伐木特许经营，其中部分获得了生态认证。从理论上讲，持有伐木特许权和获得生态认证都可能增加或减少森林损失。针对这些干预措施（其目标在于影响森林结果，但并非总是出于保护目的），现有的影响估计十分稀少，且结果好坏参半，这并不令人意外。我们探讨：加入不同的森林遥感传感器、不同的森林结果指标以及森林背景的差异，能否为未认证伐木特许经营的森林影响及生态认证的效果提供新的认识。我们利用包括森林退化在内的新全球数据，在秘鲁亚马逊地区估计了这些干预措施的森林影响，并按木材产区进行区分，以允许不同背景下影响的异质性。结果证实，在对三个区域取平均值时，未认证的伐木特许经营并未增加森林砍伐（相对于未受干预的森林），这与以往研究结果一致。然而，区分各产区能为政策和外部效度提供更多启示：在这三个核心伐木区中压力较大的一个区域，未认证特许经营使森林砍伐率出现了更大幅度的下降。退化数据提供了进一步的见解：未认证特许经营并未使森林向退化状态的转变增加，但减少了从退化状态向被砍伐状态的转变。生态认证在各类背景和各类结果中均未减少森林砍伐或退化。

title: Forest Concessions and Eco-Certifications in the Peruvian Amazon: Deforestation Impacts of Logging Rights and Restrictions
venue: Journal of Environmental Economics and Management
abstract: Concessions that grant logging rights to firms support economic development, based on forest resources. Eco-certifications place sustainability restrictions on the operation of such logging concessions. Using a spatially detailed panel and new DID estimators, we estimate the 2002-2018 impacts on forests in the Peruvian Amazon of both logging concessions and eco-certifications. We find that concessions — which have ambiguous priors —did not raise forest loss and, if anything, reduced it slightly by warding off temporary rises in external deforestation. While eco-certifications could reduce forest loss, we find no significant impact.
abstract_zh: 授予企业伐木权的特许经营，以森林资源为基础支持经济发展。生态认证对此类伐木特许经营的运营施加可持续性限制。利用空间细化的面板数据和新的DID估计量，我们估计了2002–2018年伐木特许经营与生态认证对秘鲁亚马逊森林的影响。我们发现，特许经营（其事前影响方向并不确定）并未增加森林损失，若有影响，还略微减少了森林损失，因为它遏制了外部砍伐在短期内的临时增加。虽然生态认证可能减少森林损失，但我们未发现显著影响。
